...to be equal; wherefore they seemed to us to bring toward [the body] from the inhalation, the body dying, the bones of the thorax being more [porous]... of the arteries and all the bodies contained by the <term>pneuma</term> <gloss>breath/spirit</gloss>, it is already possible to know their composition from the blood when [they] have been constructed. Therefore, the aforementioned power, the <term>aphranis</term> <gloss>loss of smell/insensitivity</gloss>, under [the conditions] of movement by the body... it is necessary to know that above the ribs is [the place] where they [are]... and according to the [part] after the height of the phlegm, the [part] upright as the beginning to be carried toward it, it is necessary; and the outgrowth beginning under the cavity that sent forth the [vessel] branch, takes its beginning from the aforementioned [things], and they arrive also [to] the part toward the heart; whence Hippocrates also says [it] carries to the principles and the internal isthmuses, and from exercise, therefore, as if [of] parts and many things being armed, the grace owed to nature. For through this we know how all the sufferings of the arteries are sent forth; and as many other things as happen similarly to all the arteries, to the most excellent bodies and to the weaker ones, and the seams, but also in the secretions, so as to make them as it has been said, because of the individual composition, moving according to the root, the whole movement of the parts of the thorax and the position of the bones of the thorax. And again, the natural passage to the spongy [parts] is [such] because of this, [nature] makes, when the flow of phlegm descends because of the virtue [of the parts] from the internal [parts] of the respiratory [organs] already. Stopping, therefore, of them, especially as many as are viscous, and [the flow] over them [is] falling under the <term>pneuma</term> <gloss>breath</gloss> and the body of the path to the arteries. For also the phlegm, being forced down in the passage of the inhalations, being breathed out, is poured out more violently through the nostrils. But it is necessary to know these, [those] assuming the voice itself to use it, the breath, the one [part] again is poured out without foam into the thorax and from the spirit, but it does not depart to the rest. It is necessary, he says, for this membrane to sit in the [part] of the whole phlegm.

translation:
The power of the emanations of the Perfect Buddha <note>original: "Samyaksambuddha"</note> dispels all obscurations through the mere hearing of his name. He is the lamp of refuge, pervasive and limitless in his enlightened activity. He is spontaneously established as the Buddha.

Avalokiteshvara <note>original: "Chenrezig"</note> is the clear manifestation of compassionate activity. He dwells everywhere in great power. Above the high sky in front of oneself and others, he dwells, spontaneously established. Samantabhadra gazes into the expanse. He is the master of the sky. Maitreya holds the reversal of obscurations. Likewise, the hundred-fold signs <note>the Buddha's physical marks</note> are in the name of the Lord of Gods. The Noble One of Bliss is blissful, and through hearing her, one is cleared of all obscurations. The Mother, the great Goddess, works to redeem obscurations. The deity with three faces and eight hands is the body of activity. The glorious wisdom-sign, the victorious goddess, dwells in that state. She is the manifestation of the brilliant radiance of craftsmanship.

Again, while the Blessed One was staying in Anathapindada's garden <note>Jetavana</note>, a sea captain named Ocean-Born <note>original: "Rgya mtsho skyes"</note> went to sea with a retinue of five hundred merchants. They were overtaken by the "Black Ogre Wind" <note>a storm</note> and became terrified and exhausted. The captain prayed to the six teachers, but the boat was still tossed by the wind. Other merchants cried out and prayed to a thousand gods like Gulang, Varuna <note>original: "Chu lha"</note>, and Kubera, but no one provided refuge.

Then a lay practitioner <note>original: "Dge bsnyen"</note> said, "The six teachers and other gods can do nothing for you. Go for refuge from your heart to the Buddha, the Blessed One, who is a manifest god; he will be your refuge." Then the merchants with one voice went for refuge to the Buddha.

The Blessed One, staying in Jetavana, knew this. He radiated light like the color of gold, brighter than a thousand suns, and illuminated all the merchants. He also radiated the light of loving-kindness, cultivated for a thousand eons, which gave them relief and turned back the "Black Ogre Wind." Then those merchants returned from the sea without harm. 

When they requested an invitation for the midday meal, he accepted by remaining silent. Then that householder went to his home, and that night he prepared many kinds of excellent food and drink. Rising early in the morning, he arranged the seating and sent word that it was time for the meal. The Blessed One, together with the community of monks, went to the householder's dining hall. 

When the boy <note>the hunchback mentioned on the next page</note> saw the Blessed One from a distance, great joy arose in him. With a manner of intense respect, he rose from his chair. The moment he rose from the chair, his hunched back became straight, just as it was before. Then, with even greater joy, he prostrated and touched the feet of the Buddha, saying, "The Blessed One has performed a difficult task for me; the Sugata has performed a difficult task for me."

Then the Blessed One sat upon the seat arranged in the center of the Sangha. The householder served whatever excellent food and drink they desired. And you were among the strivers for the sake of Allah the Almighty, the elite of Allah's servants about whom He said: "Indeed, My servants—you have no authority over them." You were among the pious who have the happiness of the two abodes, and you then became better than the near angels, for they have no desire calling them to the foul, nor a wicked soul. You had left this difficult, long obstacle behind you and bypassed all the hindrances to your goal. Let them not distract you <gloss>meaning they do not prevent you</gloss>, for with the seeking of help from Allah the Almighty and taking refuge in Him, He is the Guide. We ask Allah the Almighty—and He is the best to be asked—to support you and us with His success, help, and ease, for He is sufficient for every important matter and is the one whose help is sought in every difficulty. In His hand is the creation and the command, and He is over all things powerful. Perhaps this is what we intended to mention in this chapter; there is no power nor strength except with Allah, the High, the Great.

**The Fourth Obstacle: The Obstacle of Distractions**
Then you must, O seeker of worship—may Allah the Almighty grant you success—restrain the distractions that occupy you from the worship of Allah the Almighty and block their path against you, so they do not distract you from your goal. We have mentioned that they are four:
The first is **Provision** <note>original: al-rizq</note> and the soul's demand for that. Sufficiency is only found in **Trust** <note>original: al-tawakkul</note>. You must rely on Allah the Almighty regarding the matter of provision and need in every state. This is for two reasons:
One is to be free for worship and so that the truth of goodness may live for you. For whoever is not trustful <note>in God</note> must inevitably be preoccupied from the worship of Allah the Almighty because of need and

<column-break/>

hardship, greed, and the idling of that which he cannot do without. He fears no harm except the necessity of entreaty and the Holy One, Allah the Almighty, except for those upon whom He has bestowed His mercy and made them independent of all that harms them in their religious affairs. What need is there for that? For the matter is as some of the righteous said: "Piety is the easiest thing: if I wanted a thing, I left it." For the soul will comply and return for a time, and its state is as the speaker said:
"The soul is desirous if you make it desire; but if it is returned to little, it is content."
Another said:
"The soul is whatever you habituate it to; and my body bears whatever I charge it with."
Another said:
"The soul is only where the youth places it: if it aspires, it yearns; and if it is made to hope..."

When you know what we have described, you will be among the ascetic ones who desire the Afterlife. Know that whoever is named with the name of asceticism <note>original: al-zuhd</note> has not been named with a praiseworthy name <note>meaning the state is higher than the name</note>. You were among the solitary ones who are devoted to Allah the Glorified, who are the people of intimacy and the servants of the Lord of the Worlds. You would be as the speaker said:
"A group occupied themselves with their world ⁂ while a group devoted themselves to their Master.
He kept them at the door of His pleasure ⁂ and made them independent of all other creation.
As they remember what they did in the past ⁂ and He watches over those who do not remain."

<header>### Gem of Lofty Wisdom in the Word of Moses</header>

The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, used to go out into the rain when it fell and uncover his head to it so that it would touch him. He would say: "It has newly come from its Lord." Look at this knowledge of God from this Prophet; how majestic, high, and clear it is! The rain subjugated the best of humanity because of its proximity to its Lord. It was like the Messenger to whom revelation descends. It called him through its state and essence, so he went out to it to receive the divine benefit it brought from his Lord. Had he not obtained a divine benefit from it touching him, he would not have gone out to it. This is the message of the water from which God made "every living thing" <note>Quran 21:30</note>. Understand this.

As for the wisdom of him being placed in the ark and cast into the river, the ark represents his <term>nasut</term> <gloss>human nature or physical body</gloss>. The river <note>original: "al-yamm"</note> represents the knowledge he obtained by means of this body. This includes what was given to him by the faculties of theoretical thought, the senses, and the imagination. None of these, nor their like, would exist for this human soul without the existence of this elemental body. 

When the soul entered this body and was commanded to manage and direct it, God made these faculties tools to reach what God intended for it in the management of this ark, within which lies the tranquility of the Lord. He was cast into the river so that he might obtain the various branches of knowledge through these faculties. Through this, He informed him that even though the spirit managing him is the king, it can only manage him through these faculties. He accompanied him with these powers existing in this human nature, which was expressed as the "ark" in the language of symbols and wisdom.

Similarly, the management of the Truth <note>original: "al-Haqq"</note> over the world is only done through the world, or through its image. He only manages it through itself, just as a child depends on the existence of a parent, effects depend on their causes, conditions on their prerequisites, results on their premises, and proofs on their evidence. All of this is part of the world, and it is the management of the Truth within it. He only manages it through it. 

When we say "or through its image," meaning the image of the world, I mean the Beautiful Names and Lofty Attributes by which the Truth named Himself and with which He is described. Every name by which He is called has a meaning and a spirit that we find within the world. Therefore, the world is also managed only through the image of the world.

For this reason, He said regarding the creation of Adam, who is the comprehensive program of the descriptions of the Divine Presence—which are the Essence, Attributes, and Acts: "God created Adam in His image." His image is nothing other than the Divine Presence. He placed within this noble summary, which is the Perfect Human <note>original: "al-Insan al-Kamil"</note>, all the divine names and the realities of everything that exists outside him in the great, separate world. He made him a spirit...

...it is possible. In such places, one can use the few to attack the many. Great forests and lush grasses are where one sets an **ambush**. Open plains and sprawling fields are where **cavalry** can support one another. Where vegetation and obstacles provide cover, **foot soldiers** can engage in combat. On the open outskirts where there is room to maneuver, allowing for both advance and retreat, one should use **long halberds** <term>Ji: a traditional Chinese polearm combining a spearhead with a side blade</term> to face the enemy.

When crossing water or spanning great distances, or when utilizing differences in elevation where the enemy cannot get close, one should use **long-range crossbows** to face them. These are all dictated by the **natural character of the terrain**.

Someone asked: "Suppose within the stockades and camps, the three armies are already at rest. If the enemy takes advantage of a lapse to launch a sudden assault and attack, what should be done at such a moment?"

**Dong** <note>Referring to Xu Dong, the author of the *Tiger Seal Scripture* (Huqian Jing)</note> replied: "Station the brave in the front and hide the timid in the rear.
